data.long_meaning: The name Jadalise is derived from the Hebrew word 'Yadah', which means 'to praise'. In the Bible, the name Judah, from which Jadalise is derived, means 'praise'. Therefore, Jadalise can be understood as 'Judah's praise'.

in_hebrew.name: יגדליס
in_hebrew.long_meaning: השם יגדליס הוא שילוב של המילים העבריות 'גדל' ו'אלוהים', שפירושן אלוהים הוא גדול ורם. השם מבטא את גדלותו ורוממותו של אלוהים ומשמש כהצהרת אמונה באלוהים.

in_greek.name: Ιαδαλίση
in_greek.long_meaning: Το όνομα Ιαδαλίση προέρχεται από τις ελληνικές λέξεις 'ια' και 'δαλ', που σχετίζονται με τη θεία μεγαλοσύνη και την ανύψωση του Θεού. Το όνομα αυτό εκφράζει την πίστη στη δύναμη και τη μεγαλοσύνη του Θεού.

in_latin.name: Jadalise
in_latin.long_meaning: Nomen Jadalise derivatur ex vocibus hebraicis 'Gadol' et 'El', quae significant Deum Magnum et Excelsum. Hoc nomen est confessio fidei in Deum qui est magnus et excelsus.

historical_references.reference: Jadalise was a famous Coptic monk and scholar who lived during the 6th century in Egypt. He was known for his deep knowledge of the Scriptures and his spiritual wisdom. His teachings greatly influenced the Coptic Orthodox Church and continue to be studied by scholars today.

Another reference to Jadalise comes from the 13th century when he was mentioned in a Syriac text as one of the three great saints of the Syriac tradition, along with Mar Abhai and Mar Quriaqos. This text indicates that Jadalise was revered in the Syriac-speaking communities of the Middle East, not just in Egypt where he lived.
